name: Fleeing police vehicle (ordinary)
officialTitle: FLEEING OR ATTEMPTING TO ELUDE POLICE OFFICER; OFFENSE.
conduct: Operating a motor vehicle and WILFULLY failing or refusing to stop, fleeing, or attempting to elude a PURSUING police vehicle after a visual or audible stop signal. The signal may be by hand, voice, emergency light or siren. The officer must be in uniform with the badge prominently displayed, and the police vehicle must bear law-enforcement-agency insignia, whether or not it has an emergency light. A signal alone without these conditions does not establish this particular offense. Subtitle C generally applies to highway operation under §542.001; a different offense may have different territorial and conduct predicates. This is not an automatic substitute for Penal Code §38.04 evading arrest or detention, whose separate elements and grades remain distinct. This choice does not include the (d) reckless imminent-serious-injury-danger finding. Section 542.004 exempts persons/vehicles actually engaged in highway work unless specifically covered, but applies while traveling to or from that work.
penalty: Class B misdemeanor: ordinarily up to 180 days in jail, a fine up to $2,000, or both. Qualifying repeat-conviction findings require separate analysis; none is presumed. H.B. 1831 clarified the police-vehicle insignia requirement effective September 1, 2009; the (d)/(e) danger and presumption provisions predate that amendment; earlier conduct requires the applicable earlier law.

name: Fleeing police vehicle (reckless imminent serious-injury danger)
officialTitle: FLEEING OR ATTEMPTING TO ELUDE POLICE OFFICER; OFFENSE.
conduct: Operating a motor vehicle and WILFULLY failing or refusing to stop, fleeing, or attempting to elude a PURSUING police vehicle after a visual or audible stop signal. Subtitle C generally applies to highway operation under §542.001; a different offense may have different territorial and conduct predicates. This is not an automatic substitute for Penal Code §38.04 evading arrest or detention, whose separate elements and grades remain distinct. During commission of the fleeing offense the actor must also recklessly engage in conduct placing ANOTHER in IMMINENT danger of SERIOUS bodily injury. Actual injury is not required. Under (e), knowingly operating while intoxicated during the offense creates a presumption of that reckless danger; intoxication follows §49.01 (impaired faculties or qualifying alcohol concentration), not merely alcohol consumption. Section 2.05(a) requires the predicate facts beyond a reasonable doubt and permits, but does not require, the jury inference; other elements still require proof. Section 542.004 exempts persons/vehicles actually engaged in highway work unless specifically covered, but applies while traveling to or from that work.
penalty: Class A misdemeanor: ordinarily up to one year in jail, a fine up to $4,000, or both. Qualifying repeat-conviction findings require separate analysis; none is presumed. H.B. 1831 clarified the police-vehicle insignia requirement effective September 1, 2009; the (d)/(e) danger and presumption provisions predate that amendment; earlier conduct requires the applicable earlier law.

name: Highway fixture/landscaping collision (notify duty; damage under $200)
officialTitle: DUTY ON STRIKING STRUCTURE, FIXTURE, OR HIGHWAY LANDSCAPING.
conduct: The operator is involved in a collision resulting ONLY in damage to a structure adjacent to a highway, or a fixture or landscaping legally on or adjacent to a highway. Failing to take REASONABLE STEPS to locate and notify the owner or person in charge of the collision, the operator’s name and address, and the registration number of the vehicle driven. This is a reasonable-steps duty, not a promise that the owner must actually be found. The grade in (b) uses damage to ALL FIXTURES AND LANDSCAPING, less than $200. The grading clause does not expressly say all property or structures; this choice does not resolve a structure-only valuation question. Section 550.001 limits chapter applicability to the specified district road, qualifying business/private paid-parking access, or highway/other public place; private residential access is excluded from the private-access extension. Injury, death or damage to attended vehicles invokes different duties and is not silently treated as this property-only branch. The statute’s silence about a mental-state label does not itself establish every offense element from damage alone; applicable Penal Code §§1.03(b),6.02 and 6.03 remain relevant.
penalty: Class C misdemeanor: ordinarily a fine up to $500, without confinement as the ordinary punishment. H.B. 2190 replaced accident terminology with collision effective September 1, 2023; it did not create these grades. Earlier conduct requires its applicable version.

name: License plate (plate issued for another vehicle; ordinary fine)
officialTitle: WRONG, FICTITIOUS, ALTERED, OR OBSCURED LICENSE PLATE.
conduct: Attaching to or displaying on a motor vehicle a license plate with this condition: The plate was issued for a DIFFERENT motor vehicle. This choice uses the ordinary fine-only (b) grade, without the finding that the owner knowingly altered or made identification marks illegible. A proven owner-alteration finding changes the grade to Class B. Subsection (c)’s exclusions apply to (a)(7): normally/customarily installed trailer hitches, wheelchair lifts/carriers and bicycle/motorcycle racks; a transponder attached as its issuing authority requires; and a trailer being towed. These are not blanket exceptions to every subsection. Under (d), the court MAY dismiss eligible (a)(3),(5),(6) or (7) charges if the defect is remedied before the first court appearance, the defendant pays a reimbursement fee up to $10, and shows a department-issued plate was attached establishing registration for the offense period. Dismissal is discretionary and these conditions are cumulative; (a)(1) and fictitious plates under (a)(4) are not included.
penalty: Misdemeanor with a specific statutory maximum fine of $200; it is not a generic $500 fine. No confinement is specified for this ordinary branch. The ordinary (b) scheme is subject to the separate fictitious-plate (e) and obscured-letter/number/color (f) rules; neither is folded into this branch.
